html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. AI: artificial intelligence; RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation

  • One-page decision tables for each domain
  • The names, numbers and limits worth memorizing
  • The distractor patterns that make wrong answers attractive

2Decision Chooser

D1 Prompting and D2 Output Evaluation (35%)

Situation Best move Deciding question
Generic or weak answer Add goal, audience, context, format, constraints, example Did the prompt say what a good result is?
Big, multi-part request Decompose: plan, parts, combine, review Can each step be checked?
Output not right Specific feedback, change one thing, keep what works Which exact thing should change?
Thread drifted or very long Summarize and restart Are early decisions being lost?
Brainstorm Many varied options, judge later Is quantity the goal?
Factual or analytic task Sources, assumptions, shown figures, verify Can I check it?
Confident claim, citation, number Verify in the primary source; recalculate Where is the evidence?
Same message, different readers Adapt delivery, keep facts Did any fact change?
High stakes, people, regulated, external Qualified human review (and disclosure) Who is accountable?
Reusable, editable deliverable Artifact or file; data for another tool: structured table Will it be edited, reused or shared?

D3 Product and Model Selection (12%)

Situation Best move
Single current fact Web search
Hard reasoning, no web needed Extended thinking
Comprehensive cited report Research
Questions about your files Upload (PDF up to 1,000 pages; 100 pages for visuals)
Recurring background Project
High-volume simple tasks Haiku-type: fast, low cost
Everyday work Sonnet-type: balanced
Complex, nuanced, long work Opus-type (or the top tier): capable, slower
Routine task Lower effort; hard task: higher effort or thinking
Context crowded Restart or summarize; persist stable facts in Projects, memory, documents

D4 Workflow and D5 Configuration (28%)

Situation Best move
Vague business complaint Clarify into requirements, list assumptions, validate with people
Choosing use cases High value, low risk first; human review where errors matter
Plan from Claude Check against real capacity; ask for options
Improving a process Map, find bottlenecks, redesign, pilot, measure
Add Claude to a workflow Augment a step with draft-and-review first; redesign after a pilot
API, agents, systems integration, security architecture Escalate to Developer or Architect with a brief
Tell stakeholders Evidence-based value and plain limits, review plan
Standing instructions and knowledge Project; instructions with role, audience, format, rules, source of truth, uncertainty, escalation
Repeatable method Skill (trusted sources)
Live data in Drive or Gmail Connector, narrow scope, approvals
Policy or product changes Update knowledge and instructions, test, tell the team, version

D6 Governance (15%) and D7 Troubleshooting (10%)

Situation Best move
Personal or regulated data Remove or anonymize, minimize, approved tool and account, follow policy
Hiring, credit, benefits, medical, legal Qualified human decides; bias review; disclose AI use
Fake reviews, deception, unauthorized access Decline
Policy silent Ask the policy owner, Legal or Privacy
Data exposed Contain, report, record
Output weak Diagnose: observe, pattern, cause, change one thing, test
Claude claims an action Check the destination; is there an integration?
Slow or limit reached Lower effort or lighter model, fewer tools, new short chat, wait for reset
Optimize a workflow Baseline, change one thing, pilot, compare; standardize with templates, Projects, Skills
Exam tip

When two options both work, prefer the one that verifies, protects data, fits the task and keeps a person accountable.

3Names and Values to Know

Item Value
Exam CCAO-F; 60 items; 120 min; 720 of 1,000; USD 99; valid 12 months
Domain weights D2 21 · D4 16 · D6 15 · D1 14 · D3 12 · D5 12 · D7 10
Models Haiku fast and low cost · Sonnet balanced · Opus most capable of the three
Research 5 or more lookups, about 1 to 3 minutes, cited report, paid plans
Free-plan Projects 5
RAG for Projects Paid plans; up to about 10x capacity
Chat file limits 20 files, 500 MB each, PDF up to 1,000 pages (visuals analyzed up to 100 pages)
Project files About 30 MB each
Created files About 30 MB
Usage limits Five-hour session limit and weekly limits on paid plans
Incognito Not in history, memory or training; outside Projects; kept 30 days
Memory On by default (individual plans); per-Project memory; sensitive topics off by default
Artifacts Private by default; Docs, Slides, Design, Dashboards (beta); storage 20 MB text only
Skills Folder with a description (200 characters max) and instructions; need code execution
Connectors Your permissions; approval for send, share, trash; Auto, Always available, On demand
Exam tip

Numbers matter most where they decide a feature choice: Research is for five or more lookups, a Project holds standing background, and incognito is not an exemption from policy.

[Verify live] Plan names, limits, model names and menu labels change; the principles behind them are what the questions test.

4Distractor Patterns

Pattern Why it is tempting Why it fails
"Claude sounded confident, so send it" Fluent text feels reliable Confidence is not evidence; verify
"Ask Claude if it is sure" Quick Not independent validation
"Always use the biggest model / highest effort" More power seems safer Slower, costs usage, unnecessary
"Always use the smallest" Cheap and fast Fails on hard reasoning
"Research for everything" Sounds thorough Overkill for a simple fact
"Keep going in the same long chat" No setup Context drifts; restart or summarize
"Paste the background each time" Works today Wasteful; use a Project
"Tell Claude not to retain the data" Feels protective Not a policy control; remove or anonymize
"It's internal, so it's fine" Familiar data Internal can still be regulated or confidential
"Incognito means exempt from policy" Sounds private Policy and retention still apply
"Let Claude decide people matters" Fast Needs qualified human and disclosure
"Hide AI use" Avoids questions Transparency is expected
"Build the integration yourself" Eager Escalate API and architecture work
"Rewrite everything" Feels thorough Change one thing and retest
"Skip review to save time" Efficiency Efficiency without quality is not optimization
Exam tip

A distractor often sounds efficient (skip the check, paste everything, use the biggest model); the correct answer is usually the one that keeps quality, data safety and accountability.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Prompt Goal · context · audience · format · constraints · example
Work Decompose · iterate with specific feedback · adapt to task type
Evaluate Accurate · complete · consistent · unbiased · verified outside Claude
Review Scale with stakes; qualified human for high-risk uses
Features Web search (fact) · thinking (reasoning) · Research (report) · files · Projects · artifacts · Skills · connectors
Models Haiku fast/cheap · Sonnet balanced · Opus capable; match to task
Context Restart · summarize · persist
Config Project (background) · Skill (procedure) · connector (live data); maintain and test
Governance Policy first · classify data · minimize · human accountable · transparency
Fix Diagnose, change one thing, test
Optimize Lighter and reusable and measured, with review kept
